title: Hidden Layer
body:
Any layer that is neither the [[Input Layer]] nor the [[Output Layer]]. "Hidden" means nothing more
than that: its values are never observed in the data, they exist only as intermediate results of a
[[Forward Pass]], and nothing in the training set says what they should be.

That last point is what [[Back Propagation]] is for. The [[Loss Function]] only sees the output, so
there is no direct error signal for a hidden unit; its gradient has to be assembled from the
gradients of everything downstream of it, which is exactly the [[Chain Rule]] sum that
backpropagation computes. A network with no hidden layers ([[Perceptron]],
[[Logistic Regression]]) needs none of that machinery.

**Depth is hidden layers, and depth is only worth anything with a non-linear
[[Activation Function]].** Two linear layers compose to one linear layer, so without $\sigma$ a
hundred hidden layers have the expressive power of zero. See [[Non-Linear]]. Given a non-linearity,
one sufficiently wide hidden layer can already approximate any continuous function to any accuracy
(the universal approximation result), which sounds like it makes depth pointless. It does not: the
required *width* can be astronomically large, while stacking layers gets the same functions with
far fewer [[Weights]]. Depth buys efficiency, not reachability.

The usual reading of what they compute is a feature hierarchy: early layers pick up small local
patterns, later ones combine those into larger ones. In a [[CNN]] on images this is visible and
well documented (edges, then textures, then object parts). In a plain
[[Multilayer Perceptron]] it is a much looser story, so do not oversell it.

Practical shape notes: the number of hidden layers and their widths are **hyperparameters**, chosen
before training rather than learned, and each hidden layer of $n$ units over $m$ inputs adds
$n \times m$ weights plus $n$ [[Bias Term|biases]]. [[ReLU]] is the default activation for hidden
layers; [[Sigmoid]] belongs on the output when you want a probability.

## Related

- [[Input Layer]], [[Output Layer]]: the two that are not hidden
- [[Multilayer Perceptron]]: a network defined by having at least one of these
- [[Back Propagation]], [[Non-Linear]], [[Activation Function]]
- [[CNN]]: hidden layers with structure imposed on them
